subject: Question: default capture window for inputs vs generated outputs (AtlasMed)
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@atlasmed.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: AtlasMed Security <security@atlasmed.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify default capture window for inputs vs generated outputs

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — AtlasMed is excited about the potential to use Redwood for our patient triage assistant. Before procurement finishes, our security team needs a concise answer on what Redwood keeps by default. Can you confirm the following for the hosted API in the US region?

- What is the default retention window for raw requests (user prompts / inputs)?
- What is the default retention window for model-generated outputs (responses and streaming fragments)?
- Are streaming token buffers (partial stream fragments) treated differently from finalized outputs?
- Is there an option to mark a session as "ephemeral" so prompts are not persisted at all?

Our security reviewers want this documented for the risk assessment. I attached our questionnaire (atlasmed_security_qs.xlsx) — we highlighted the retention-related rows.

Could you reply with the short answers we can drop into the form? Appreciate it.

— Maria
Maria Lopez
Head of Product Security, AtlasMed
maria.lopez@atlasmed.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@atlasmed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, AtlasMed Security <security@atlasmed.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 18:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify default capture window for inputs vs generated outputs

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. Short answers first (for your form), followed by a brief explanation and next steps below.

Short answers (US hosted):
- Default retention for raw requests (prompts/inputs): 30 days by default.
- Default retention for model-generated final outputs: 90 days by default.
- Streaming token buffers (partial fragments): ephemeral by design — persisted only for the duration of the session and included in temporary buffers that are retained up to 7 days for debugging if not finalized.
- Ephemeral session flag: yes — we support a per-request "no_store=true" flag that prevents writes to persistent stores (prompts and outputs are not retained beyond transient execution).

More detail:
- Purpose & tiers: the 30/90 split exists to balance operational needs (short-term debugging, quality monitoring) with data minimization. Requests are considered higher-sensitivity inputs and have the shorter horizon. Finalized outputs are kept longer to support customer troubleshooting, billing reconciliation, and quality-eval hooks.
- Streaming vs final: streaming fragments are kept only as transient buffers unless a stream completes and produces a finalized transcript; in that case the finalized transcript is treated as a "final output" and follows the 90-day path. If a stream errors, fragments are scrubbable and removed according to the 7-day ephemeral buffer policy.
- Ephemeral requests: the no_store flag bypasses all persistence tiers. Note: some platform features (model evals, usage analytics) may be unavailable when no_store is used; this is documented in the API reference (see link I pasted below).

I'll attach a concise retention matrix (Retention_Matrix_v2.pdf) that maps each artifact type to storage horizon, default residency, and erasure path. If you want, Karthik and I can fill the highlighted lines in your spreadsheet and return it as a completed PDF for your security team.

Action: can you confirm what fields in the spreadsheet should be considered authoritative (AtlasMed security vs procurement)? Once you confirm, we'll annotate and return.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, AtlasMed Security <security@atlasmed.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Jul 2028 09:47:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify default capture window for inputs vs generated outputs

Maria — quick follow-up with implementation notes so you can map answers to your DLP controls.

- Retention enforcement: all retention windows are enforced by an automated TTL workflow. For the US hosted plane, TTL jobs run daily; items past horizon are marked for asynchronous deletion and are purged within 72 hours of the mark.
- De-dup & caching: prefix/KV caches may keep hashed prefixes for dedup and fast routing. These cache entries are not queryable as raw text and persist for up to 7 days; they are excluded from customer-exported datasets.
- Erasure requests: if AtlasMed requests a targeted erasure (by session_id or user_id), we locate artifacts across the same index and queue them for immediate deletion outside the TTL timeline; we provide a deletion confirmation report.
- Audit evidence: we can provide an export of deletion markers and job run timestamps (redacted where necessary) as part of a compliance review.

One caveat: private deployments (VPC / on-prem) default to customer-managed retention and we recommend configuring a shorter horizon if AtlasMed’s policy requires it. For hosted, the default numbers I provided are standard, but we can make a contract clause to override retention windows for your account if needed.

Happy to sync live if you want the security engineers to see the deletion runbook.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Security Integrations, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Clarify default capture window for inputs vs generated outputs

Maria — thanks for the patience. Per Grace and Karthik's notes, I filled the highlighted retention rows in your spreadsheet and attached the completed copy (see updated atlasmed_security_qs.xlsx). Summary to drop into procurement documentation: 

- Default data horizons (hosted, US): inputs/prompts: 30 days; finalized outputs: 90 days; streaming fragments: transient buffers up to 7 days.
- Ephemeral option: "no_store=true" available to prevent any persistent storage.
- Deletion evidence: AtlasMed can request immediate targeted erasure; Redwood will provide deletion confirmation and deletion-job audit trails.

If you want contractual language, we can propose a short clause for the SOW that pins the hosted retention to these numbers or reduces them for an additional compliance add-on. Next step: Maria — confirm whether security or procurement should sign off on the annotated spreadsheet; once you indicate, we'll send the PDF and a one-page runbook for your audit team.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
